subject: History
topic: Indian Independence Act 1947 and Partition — mixed tiers
description: Mountbatten Plan, 3 June Plan, partition, Radcliffe Line, princely-state integration

questions.stem: The INDIAN INDEPENDENCE ACT, 1947 was passed by which legislature?

options.option_text: The Indian Constituent Assembly meeting at Delhi
The British Parliament at Westminster, London
The Imperial Legislative Council in colonial Delhi
The All India Congress Committee at Bombay

questions.explanation: Indian Independence Act 1947 — passed by the British Parliament; received Royal Assent on 18 July 1947. Provided for the partition of British India into two independent dominions (India + Pakistan) on 15 August 1947. Both dominions free to write their own constitutions. The Act ended British paramountcy over princely states (~565 of them), giving them choice to accede to either dominion or remain independent. Distractor 1 — Constituent Assembly drafted India's Constitution (Jan 1950), not the 1947 Act. Distractor 3 — Imperial Legislative Council was abolished by then. Distractor 4 — AICC is a Congress body, not a legislature.

questions.stem: The 'Mountbatten Plan' announced on 3 June 1947 proposed:

options.option_text: Continuation of direct British rule for ten more years across India
Partition of British India into two new dominions with princely choice
Direct annexation of all the princely states by Britain itself
A federal Indian dominion functioning under the British Crown only

questions.explanation: 3 June Plan — Lord Mountbatten (last Viceroy, arrived 24 March 1947). Announced partition of British India into India + Pakistan; PRINCELY STATES given choice to join either dominion or remain independent (subsequently nearly all integrated, with exceptions: Hyderabad — annexed via Operation Polo 1948; Junagadh — plebiscite + accession 1948; Jammu & Kashmir — accession after Pakistani tribal incursion, October 1947). Bengal + Punjab partitioned. Plan accepted by Congress + Muslim League. Implemented via the Indian Independence Act 1947.

questions.stem: The boundary between India and Pakistan was drawn by a commission headed by:

options.option_text: Lord Mountbatten, the last Viceroy of India
Cyril Radcliffe, a British lawyer who had not visited India
Stafford Cripps, the leader of the Cripps Mission
Pethick Lawrence, head of the Cabinet Mission

questions.explanation: RADCLIFFE LINE — drawn by Cyril Radcliffe, a British lawyer with no prior knowledge of India, in just 5 weeks (June-Aug 1947). He chaired two boundary commissions (one for Bengal, one for Punjab), each with 4 members (2 Congress + 2 ML). He resolved deadlocks alone. The boundary was announced on 17 August 1947 (TWO DAYS AFTER independence), causing massive last-minute uncertainty + violence. Resulted in one of the largest mass migrations in history (~14-18 million displaced) and the deaths of ~1-2 million in communal violence. Radcliffe never visited India again; said he'd 'never do it again'.

questions.stem: The integration of princely states into the Indian Union was masterminded by:

options.option_text: Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first Prime Minister
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, with V.P. Menon as Secretary
Maulana Azad, the first Education Minister
Dr B.R. Ambedkar, the chief drafter of the Constitution

questions.explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel — Home Minister + States Department head; nicknamed the 'Iron Man of India'. With V.P. Menon (Secretary to the States Department), he persuaded most of ~565 princely states to ACCEDE to India by 15 August 1947 via the 'Instrument of Accession' on three subjects (Defence, External Affairs, Communications). Hard cases: HYDERABAD (annexed via Operation POLO, Sep 1948), JUNAGADH (plebiscite, 1948), JAMMU & KASHMIR (acceded after tribal invasion, October 1947). Statue of Unity in Gujarat (182 m, world's tallest) honours Patel.

questions.stem: The CABINET MISSION (1946) — which preceded independence — proposed an arrangement that did NOT include:

options.option_text: A three-tiered union of British India and princely states
Immediate full partition of India into India and Pakistan
A grouping system for provinces along religious-majority lines
A constituent assembly to draft a constitution for united India

questions.explanation: Cabinet Mission (March-June 1946) — sent by the Attlee Labour government; consisted of Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander. PROPOSED: a UNITED India with three GROUPS of provinces (A = Hindu majority, B = Muslim-majority west, C = Muslim-majority east); a weak federal centre handling defence, foreign affairs, communications; provinces could opt out after 10 years. Did NOT propose partition. Initially accepted by Congress + ML but ML withdrew over interpretation. Direct Action Day (16 Aug 1946) — Calcutta riots → confirmed partition unavoidable. Cabinet Mission is the LAST significant unification attempt.

questions.stem: Pakistan was founded on the basis of the TWO-NATION THEORY, propounded principally by:

options.option_text: Mahatma Gandhi during the early Civil Disobedience movement
Muhammad Ali Jinnah, leader of the All-India Muslim League
Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, founder of Aligarh Muslim University
Allama Iqbal, the philosopher-poet of British India

questions.explanation: Two-nation theory — Hindus and Muslims constitute two distinct nations. Earliest articulated by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan (late 19th century, Aligarh Movement) and refined by Allama Iqbal (Allahabad Address, 1930). But CHIEFLY championed politically by MUHAMMAD ALI JINNAH from the late 1930s onward as Quaid-i-Azam of the Muslim League. Lahore Resolution (1940) demanded a separate Muslim homeland. Distractor 3 — Sir Syed FORESHADOWED but didn't politically demand partition. Distractor 4 — Iqbal articulated the idea poetically but Jinnah converted it into political reality.

questions.stem: PARTITION violence was severe in which two provinces in particular?

options.option_text: Madras Presidency and Bombay Presidency in the south
Punjab and Bengal, both partitioned along communal lines
United Provinces and Bihar in the Hindi heartland
North-West Frontier Province and Sindh in the west

questions.explanation: Punjab and Bengal — both had MIXED populations and were partitioned along the Radcliffe Line, leaving large minorities on the wrong side. Resulted in MASS MIGRATIONS (~10-12 million in Punjab alone) and HORRIFIC violence (1-2 million estimated dead, mass rapes, abductions). Punjab's western half went to Pakistan (capital Lahore); eastern half to India (capital eventually Chandigarh). Bengal split as well: West Bengal (India, capital Calcutta/Kolkata) + East Bengal (East Pakistan, became Bangladesh in 1971). Distractor 1, 3 didn't see partition violence. Distractor 4 went entirely to Pakistan, less internal violence.
